To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

long-lived exotic strongly-interacting massive particles (SIMPs) can destroy the primordial 7Be and the 7Li abundances in the scenario of Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBNs), and that the 7Be and Li problems can be solved if the SIMPs are sub-strongly interacting.
the 7Be and/or 7Li abundance can be suppressed in the BBN scenario with long-lived sub-SIMP X if the X is weakly interacting with nucleons and the mass of X is smaller than 10 TeV.
long-lived sub-SIMP can explain the observed 7Li abundance in metal-poor halo star observations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible signatures of long-lived exotic massive particles on the abundances of light elements in BBN.
the possible existence of long-lived exotic particles and the signatures on light element abundancies in the early universe.
a possible solution of the 7Li abundance problem by the existence of long-lived sub-SIMP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 7 Li problem is solved by the long-lived sub-SIMP scenario if the mass of the X is larger than 10 4 GeV.
the 7 Li problem can be solved by the existence of long-lived sub-SIMP with mass of about 1-10 GeV and interaction strength of about 1/3 of that of the strong interaction.
the 7Be and the 7Li destructions are possible, but the 7Li abundance predicted by the standard model is not necessarily excluded by the current observational data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
long-lived sub-SIMP is a candidate for a solution of the 7Li abundance problem.
the 7Be and the 7Li abundances in the standard BBN model are not robust, and that they are sensitive to long-lived sub-SIMP scenarios.
long-lived sub-SIMP with mass of order 1 GeV and interaction strength between an nucleon and an X of order 0.2 GeV would be a solution of the 7Li abundance problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
long-lived exotic strongly-interacting massive particles can have significant impact on the light element abundances.
a new type of exotic particles can affect light element abundances in BBN.
a long-lived sub-SIMP can be a candidate for a new physics which solves the 7Li abundance problem.
